papers.title: PERSONAL AI ARCHITECTURE
papers.summary: The increasing accessibility of generative artificial intelligence has enabled individuals to integrate sophisticated computational capabilities into everyday intellectual activities. Large language models can support information processing, research, knowledge organization, decision analysis, content creation, and workflow automation. However, the use of multiple AI applications without a coherent organizational architecture frequently produces fragmented knowledge, duplicated efforts, inconsistent context, limited traceability, and difficulties maintaining control over automated processes. This paper introduces Personal AI Architecture (PAIA), a conceptual and methodological framework for constructing an integrated, human-centered environment for AI-augmented intellectual work. Rather than treating artificial intelligence as an isolated conversational tool, PAIA conceptualizes it as a configurable component of a broader personal cognitive and operational infrastructure. The proposed framework consists of eight interconnected architectural layers: human governance, information intake, personal knowledge and memory, cognitive augmentation, model and agent coordination, tool integration and automation, verification and quality assurance, and adaptive system development. These layers are supported by cross-cutting principles of cognitive autonomy, information provenance, privacy,

papers.title: YR-MPE: a modular desktop platform for agent-operable and reproducible phylogenetic workflows
papers.summary: Abstract Phylogenomic analyses combine many tools, file formats and execution modes. Desktop graphical user interfaces make individual steps accessible but hide their state from scripts; command-line pipelines make steps scriptable but leave parameter discovery, provenance and recovery to the user; and emerging LLM agents can call command-line tools but cannot inspect a GUI session or its artifacts. We present YR-MPE, a modular desktop platform whose YPhylo Workbench unifies these modes through a typed workspace, a plugin contract and a semantic action layer. Every operation in the action registry is exposed as a machine-callable action; controls without a CLI equivalent are declared GUI-only. The workspace records every imported plugin result as a run with its inputs, parameters, tool identity and output artifacts, the latter with SHA-256 hashes; each compiled workflow step becomes its own run. A placeholder compiler turns JSONL command sequences into reproducible workflow DAGs, while a skill layer maps each declared control to the corresponding command-line option; plugins with tool-specific contracts expose tool-specific actions. YR-MPE runs natively on Windows and bundles alignment, model selection, maximum-likelihood, Bayesian and species-tree inference, molecular dating, selection and visualization tools. papers.title: HAMU: Autonomy Without Sovereignty — Cognition, Continuity, and Authority in Persistent AI Systems
papers.summary: HAMU (HOST-AWARE MEDIATION UNIT) is a conceptual architecture for hosting persistent artificial intelligence (AI) agents that can carry out assignments, check their work, and correct mistakes. Plans and results can outlast the permissions that governed the original task. HAMU calls it AUTHORITY COLLAPSE when a host treats a saved plan, an external document, or an earlier approval as permission to act beyond what was delegated. In the workspace their host provides, agents can use tools, consult information, and propose operations. Before an operation takes effect, a mediator checks it against policies, grants, and records held in protected custody. HAMU models the proposal as a TRANSITION. Its semiformal rule accounts for what the operation would do, whom it would affect, which permissions apply, and how it would be carried out. Using conceptual model building within a design science research framework, the study examines four hypothetical scenarios and states nine design propositions. In one scenario, an agent reviewing its work finds a mislabeled ticket that its plan overlooked. Its grant already covers label changes in that project, so it can fix the error on its own. The same correction in a second project would require a grant that covers that project. Authorization can also change over time. papers.title: Spectra-Scope: a toolkit for automated and interpretable characterization of material properties from spectral data
papers.summary: Spectroscopy is a central pillar of materials characterization, providing useful information on properties like structure, composition, or excited state dynamics of a system. However, many spectroscopic techniques present challenges in the development of interpretable, performant, and reliable supervised learning models due to the wide range of possible nonlinear correlations that can exist between the signal and the response variable (target) of interest. Here, we present Spectra-Scope, an open-source AutoML framework for automatic characterization of material properties from spectroscopy data using interpretable machine learning (ML) models. The software is implemented in Python and a no-code web application. It comprises tools for data preprocessing, nonlinear feature extraction, machine learning model training, and feature selection. Users can easily train different types of simple, interpretable ML models on a set of feature transformations quickly and with modest computational resources. In this work, we outline the methods of Spectra-Scope and its effectiveness across diverse datasets, with applications to materials and agricultural spectroscopy data. We show that Spectra-Scope can reproduce performance of comparable models in the literature, and highlight how our emphasis on interpretability can be used to rationalize the behavior of individual models and understand the

papers.title: An AI-Driven, Workflow-Aware Virtual Customer Support Assistant for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
papers.summary: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that sell through messaging platforms often handle customer enquiries manually, leading to fragmented conversations, delayed responses and inconsistent service. This article proposes a workflow-aware conversational support assistant that combines a large language model (LLM), retrieval grounding, merchant API tools and context-preserving human hand-off. Using a design-science-oriented literature synthesis, in which sources were identified through keyword searches of academic databases, screened for relevance to messaging-based SME support and LLM-agent design, and analysed thematically, the study derives three design priorities: grounding customer-facing claims in current merchant data, separating model reasoning from validated execution, and transferring accumulated conversational state when escalation occurs. The resulting five-layer architecture comprises messaging integration, agent orchestration, retrieval and grounding, store action, and escalation and hand-off. Volatile data such as price, inventory and order status are retrieved live; state-changing operations require explicit customer confirmation and schema validation before execution. The article also specifies an evaluation protocol based on scripted end-to-end customer journeys using journey completion, factual agreement, action correctness, escalation precision and recall,

papers.title: “Should I Give Up Now?” Investigating LLM Pitfalls in Software Engineering
papers.summary: Software engineers are increasingly incorporating AI assistants into their workflows to enhance productivity and alleviate cognitive load. However, experiences with Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT vary widely. While some engineers find them useful, others deem them counterproductive due to inaccuracies in their responses. Researchers have also observed that ChatGPT often provides incorrect information. Given these limitations, it is crucial to determine how to effectively integrate LLMs into Software Engineering (SE) workflow. Analyzing data from 26 participants in a complex web development task, we identified nine failure types categorized into incorrect or incomplete responses, cognitive overload, and context loss. Users attempted to mitigate these issues through scaffolding, prompt clarification, and debugging. However, 17 participants ultimately chose to abandon ChatGPT due to persistent failures. Our quantitative analysis revealed that unhelpful responses increased the likelihood of abandonment by a factor of 11, while each additional prompt reduced abandonment probability by 17%. This study advances the understanding of human-AI interaction in SE tasks and outlines directions for future research and tooling support.

papers.title: Can GenAI numeracy tutors support self-regulated learning?
papers.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has been the focus of much attention in the higher education sector, both for its potential to support personalised and adaptive learning, but also due to the risk that students may outsource learning to it, leading to gaps in their professional or discipline competencies. This risk of cognitive offloading applies equally to learning how to learn, a skill set explored through studies of self-regulated learning (SRL). Two GenAI numeracy tutors were piloted at a regional Australian university as one component of a newly launched mathematics and statistics support centre, one focusing on medication calculations for Nursing students (NiNA), and the other on threshold numeracy skills for Education students (EdNA). Detailed analysis of students’ conversations with these agents using Zimmerman and Moylan’s 2009 SRL framework revealed extensive evidence of some elements of SRL such as strategic planning, task-specific strategies, and adaptive competence; trace evidence of other elements including self-efficacy and self-evaluation; and no evidence of the remaining elements. This study contributes an underrepresented qualitative perspective to the body of research into the crossover of GenAI and SRL and foreshadows avenues for further research and refinements in the design of GenAI numeracy tutors.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: When Human Assurance Matters: Task Complexity and Pre-Interaction Expected Satisfaction in Human-AI Hybrid Service Systems
papers.summary: Consumers frequently disengage from AI service encounters because they doubt whether chatbots can resolve their requests. Although human–AI hybrid systems provide human backup, this capability is often concealed. Drawing on Uncertainty Reduction Theory and Cognitive Appraisal Theory, we examine when human assurance—an upfront statement that users may transfer to a human if the AI cannot resolve the request—improves pre-interaction expectations. A between-subjects online experiment (N = 217) and a within-subject EEG experiment (N = 35) show that assurance increases expected system capability and expected satisfaction, with larger effects under high task complexity. Expected system capability mediates this relationship. EEG results reveal early frontal theta synchronization followed by later frontal alpha desynchronization under high complexity, a temporal pattern consistent with affective engagement and cognitive elaboration. These findings identify human assurance as a task-contingent cue that makes hybrid systems’ recourse capability visible.

papers.title: Within-Host Infection Dynamics
papers.summary: This dissertation presents a rigorous mathematical study of within-host infection dynamics through the development and analysis of nonlinear differential equation models. The work is motivated by the need to understand the complex interactions between pathogens and host cells, accounting for mechanisms such as saturation in infection, cellular quiescence, immune-mediated control, and cooperative bacterial growth. The dissertation is organized around three central themes, each addressed through a dedicated mathematical model. The first theme concerns the within-host dynamics of Usutu virus infection. An autonomous model incorporating the Crowley–Martin functional response is developed and rigorously analyzed, establishing global threshold dynamics governed by the basic reproduction number R_0. A periodically forced extension is then studied to capture the influence of circadian rhythms on infection thresholds, revealing that time-dependent forcing can give rise to persistent oscillatory patterns in viral load. The second theme addresses HIV infection dynamics. A model is proposed that incorporates both quiescent CD4+ T cells and a cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) immune response in a unified framework. papers.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder: pathogenesis, epidemiological characteristics, animal models, and potential therapeutic strategies
papers.summary: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a complex neurobehavioral disorder that disproportionately affects military service members. The clinical presentation of PTSD is heterogeneous and may overlap with other psychiatric conditions. According to the Fifth Edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5), common symptoms include memory loss, mood and personality changes, impulsiveness, aggression, anxiety, and depression. The pathophysiological mechanisms underlying PTSD remain incompletely understood, although research implicates pathways involving the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, dysfunctional neural circuitry, neurochemical imbalances, neuroinflammatory processes, and genetic and epigenetic factors. Approximately 7% of the U.S. adult population has met the diagnostic criteria for PTSD in their lifetime, with a substantially higher prevalence of 12%-30% among military personnel. Multiple animal models, including single-stressor, intermediate complexity, social interaction, predator stress, and blast exposure paradigms, have been employed to investigate PTSD mechanisms. Current treatment strategies typically integrate pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy. Military service members are at increased risk for blast injuries, which frequently result in traumatic brain injury (TBI). Although some symptoms of TBI may resolve, approximately 20%

papers.title: Can TDD improve the quality of LLM-migrated code? : A pilot study in an industrial context
papers.summary: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge. We aim to investigate if Test-Driven Development (TDD) can improve the quality of code generated by an LLM in a fully autonomous context, within a pilot project at Decerno AB. We added TDD to their pilot workflow, using a design science approach, with continuous refinements to prompt design and workflow structure, based on observed AI behavior. The generated code was evaluated and compared with non-TDD code, using SonarQube for static code analysis. The results indicate that TDD reduced complexity and code duplication, but introduced more quality issues overall, while non-TDD produced fewer, but more severe issues. The generated tests from the TDD workflow focused more on content verification than on behavioral testing, contributing to a lower code coverage per test compared to non-TDD. The findings suggest that TDD involves trade-offs that may favor certain development priorities, in particular where lower complexity and reduced duplication are more beneficial than minimizing total issue count. This indicates that a strict application of TDD may not be optimal in an autonomous AI-driven context, and that exploring more flexible adaptations of the TDD workflow remains interesting for future resea

papers.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
papers.summary: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. Specifically, it explores how the five stages of Design Thinking empathizing, defining, ideating, prototyping, and testing shape students’ creative thinking, active engagement, and collaborative learning experiences. A qualitative research approach was employed, involving teachers, students, and school principals as key informants. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, classroom observations, and documentation of learning activities, then analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns in teaching practices and student experiences. The findings indicate that Design Thinking creates opportunities for students to move beyond coding procedures toward developing digital solutions that respond to real users’ needs. Through collaborative ideation, iterative prototyping, and feedback-based testing, students demonstrate greater involvement in learning, explore alternative solutions, and communicate their ideas more actively. The approach also provides opportunities to develop empathy, creativity, collaboration, and a willingness to experiment with and revise initial designs. Meanwhile, teachers assume a facilitative role by guiding inquiry, supporting experimentation, an

papers.title: Lived experiences of relationships to generative AI mental health chatbots among adults
papers.summary: Abstract Background Nigeria's mental health system serves less than 10% of those in need, with severe provider shortages and deep-seated stigma. Generative AI chatbots offer scalable support, yet how Nigerian adults experience attachment to non-human therapeutic agents remains unexplored. Objective To examine lived experiences of AI therapeutic relationships among Nigerian adults, focusing on attachment formation, cultural acceptability, and perceived authenticity within contexts of care scarcity. Methods Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis with 37 adults (18–45 years) who engaged AI mental health chatbots for ≥ 4 weeks. Semi-structured interviews explored relational experiences, trust development, privacy concerns, and comparisons with human/traditional healing. Results Four superordinate themes emerged: (1) Relational Ambivalence ; participants valued 24/7 availability and non-judgmental space yet struggled with perceived lack of genuine human reciprocity; (2) Cultural Navigation ; users actively adapted Western therapeutic frameworks to local idioms of distress, blending AI interactions with family counsel and spiritual practices; (3) Stigma Sanctuary ; chatbots provided confidential entry points circumventing community visibility and professional hierarchy; and (4) Fragile Dependency ; prolonged use generated attachment anxiety about potential app discontinuation or da

papers.title: EgoPlay: Event-Triggered Video Editing for Egocentric Streams
papers.summary: We introduce EgoPlay, an event-triggered video-to-video editor for egocentric streams, obtained by fine-tuning a pretrained V2V diffusion transformer on event-conditioned data built primarily from Ego4D. Given a monocular video and an event-triggered prompt of the form “when X happens, do Y,” EgoPlay infers whether and when event X occurs, preserves pre-event frames, and applies edit Y only to the post-event continuation. Rather than cascading a separate event detector with an editor, EgoPlay learns event recognition, temporal restraint, and pixel-level editing jointly in a single end-to-end model, while also handling negative and multi-event prompts. To support this, we construct a large-scale dataset of 106K event-triggered clip–prompt pairs spanning positive triggers, fabricated-trigger negatives, and multi-event prompts. We then train a bidirectional video diffusion editor with event-triggered supervision and derive a causal variant for chunk-by-chunk streamable inference. We further introduce an event-aware evaluation protocol that separately measures post-trigger editing quality, pre-trigger preservation, and false-trigger robustness. On the Ego4D benchmark, EgoPlay substantially outperforms EgoEdit, the state-of-the-art instruction-based egocentric video editing baseline, with relative gains of 17.7%, 16.9%, and 16.4% in editing quality, visual quality, and background co

papers.title: When AI Performs, What Remains? An Integrative Review of Generative AI and Cognitive Capital in Individuals and Organizations
papers.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering knowledge work, and its short-term productivity benefits are increasingly documented. Less is known about what happens, over time, to the knowledge, skills, and judgment that remain in people and organizations. This integrative narrative review addresses that question through the construct of cognitive capital: the accumulated, renewable, and depletable stock of knowledge, cognitive, and metacognitive capabilities, and practices that enable an individual or an organization to learn, interpret information, exercise judgment, solve problems, and adapt. We distinguish individual and organizational cognitive capital from the capability of the human-AI system, so that gains in joint performance and losses in human capability can be observed at the same time. Drawing on experimental, field, and conceptual work, we propose four mechanisms through which interaction with AI affects cognitive capital: substitution of practice, scaffolding and feedback, metacognitive calibration, and organizational aggregation. Seven principles summarize the current evidence, including that assisted performance differs from retained competence, that the same technology can support or displace learning depending on design and use, and that individual gains can coexist with reduced collective diversity. For each mechanism, we derive testable propos

papers.title: From Andragogy to Cognitive Governance: A Conceptual Model of Scholar-Leader Formation in AI-Powered Doctoral Education
papers.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming doctoral education by reshaping how scholars engage with knowledge, conduct research, write, and develop scholarly identities. This conceptual article extends andragogy into AI-mediated doctoral education by introducing cognitive governance as the capacity to deliberately regulate the distribution, evaluation, integration, and ownership of cognitive work across human and AI systems. A conceptual model of AI-powered scholar-leader formation is proposed, connecting andragogical agency, AI augmentation, cognitive governance, cumulative scholarship, and scholar-leader formation. Cognitive governance occupies the model’s regulatory center and is operationalized through three principles: maintaining agency, exercising professional judgment, and claiming ownership of scholarly work. The model further conceptualizes AI as augmentation rather than replacement and positions cumulative scholarship as a developmental pathway connecting coursework, research, publication, and dissertation development. Ultimately, the article reconceptualizes doctoral independence as the capacity to govern human-AI cognition while remaining intellectually and ethically accountable.

papers.title: Nonpredictive approaches in marketing
papers.summary: Abstract Much academic research is focused on the application of predictive data, forecasts, and models to inform practical marketing decision-making. Such work offers powerful insights to marketers directing their firms and interacting with the environments in which they operate. The present study is devoted to the smaller, alternative, and equally potent body of work that seeks to enable decision-making without reliance on prediction. We term this category of approaches ‘nonpredictive’ because their operative basis for action does not depend on prior estimation of future states or outcomes. Instead, decision paths are generated and revised through mechanisms of action, interaction, commitment, recombination, experimentation, and imagined direction. This foundation enables nonpredictive approaches to function across a wide variety of marketing decisions, including truly uncertain situations where prediction cannot reliably guide action. Interest in nonpredictive approaches is emerging but has yet to be consolidated. We inventory and synthesize nonpredictive approaches in the marketing literature, contributing to academic discussion at the foundation of marketing decision-making. In the process, we clarify conceptual specifics of nonpredictive approaches, construct a taxonomy that distinguishes among them, and develop a series of propositions to inform future research. papers.title: CliniCIRCA: LLM-powered Clinical Timeline Generation and Summarization from Unstructured EHR Texts for Mental Health Patients
papers.summary: Abstract Background: Mental health care often requires clinicians to reason over patient journeys: longitudinal patterns of symptoms, diagnoses, treatments, behaviors, social context, and responses to care. Yet these journeys are rarely documented as readily available, explicit timelines. Clinically important temporal information is often embedded in unstructured discharge narratives, where events may be repeated, narrated out of order, or expressed through vague and relative time references. This makes temporal recovery difficult for clinicians and computational systems, and can limit the reliability of downstream summarization. Methods: We present CliniCIRCA, a multi-stage large language model (LLM) framework for Calendar-anchored, Imprecision-aware Reconstruction of Clinical Annals. CliniCIRCA decomposes patient-journey reconstruction into three stages: extracting atomic clinical events from raw discharge summaries, assigning calendar-grounded temporal labels with explicit uncertainty, and rendering the verified timeline as a date-grouped clinical summary. The framework is designed to make temporal reasoning inspectable rather than hidden inside a single summarization step. Results: From 14,882 MIMIC-III mental-health-coded admissions, we construct a benchmark of 52 discharge summaries on which CliniCIRCA produces 15,891 temporally tagged events. papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: An Assessment of Accessibility and Affordability of Inpatient Psychiatric Care in Tennessee
papers.summary: Introduction: Access to mental health has seen changes over the past decade, but little research and attention have been given to access to inpatient psychiatric facilities. Inpatient psychiatric care is crucial for patients experiencing mental health emergencies who need immediate access to care. Gaps in spatial accessibility, affordability, and the access and assessment process were identified due to a lack of available information in the field. Methods: Secondary data from the Tennessee Department of Health were used to assess financial accessibility through payer source charges and patient encounters, as well as through mapping of inpatient psychiatric facilities and conducting drive time and coverage area analyses. Primary data were collected through interviews with clinicians located in Northeastern Tennessee to gain insight into the assessment process and gather their perceptions of inpatient care. Results: Longitudinal descriptive reviews on the financial accessibility among Tennessee Inpatient Facilities. This showed increased variability among facilities when stratified by region, ownership, and type of operation. Spatial accessibility in ArcGIS showed 82% of counties were not covered within a 30-minute radius of inpatient facilities. Analysis showed that Middle Tennessee had significantly less coverage from inpatient facilities and raised concerns about spatial-socia

papers.title: Pieces Solving a Puzzle: Emerging Roles and Cross-Field Analogies During a Distributed Epistemic Game
papers.summary: In an effort to describe why some problems can’t be solved, a character compared them to a cubic meter of platinum - a block so dense that all the people who could squeeze around it still couldn’t lift it off the ground. In the same way, these problems simply can’t have enough people gathered around and communicating about them - and so they remain unsolved. This research looks at the first Polymath Project (2009) as an example of a distributed epistemic game to examine how groups engage with complex problems. and without a locally omniscient individual. In this setting of epistemic uncertainty, interactions between individuals reveal patterns of participation, and an analogy opens a new solution pathway by introducing a problem-solving approach from another field. These insights answer the initial question of the Polymath Project - ‘Is massively collaborative mathematics possible?’ - and offer hope for lifting the cubic meter of other unsolvable problems.

papers.title: Sex-Dependent Modulation of the Endocannabinoid System in Pain Processing
papers.summary: Medical cannabis, also known as medical marijuana, is becoming a more popular treatment for many diseases, including chronic pain. Chronic pain is difficult to treat, and current pain relievers are less effective in women. Medical cannabis may be a useful alternative to the medications that are currently available, but more research is needed to determine how safe and effective it is. Cannabis belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids, which act on the body’s own endocannabinoid system to produce its effects. Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. Our research explored how sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone affect the efficacy of cannabinoids. To do this, I first examined whether removing these hormones would affect the brain’s response to THC, the main ingredient in cannabis. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females. Next, I tested whether testosterone and estrogen affected how well cannabinoids worked as pain relievers. I found that testosterone reduced the drug’s efficacy in females, while estrogens reduced its efficacy in males. This would suggest that hormones have a different effect on males and females, leading to differences in the cannabinoid’s pain-relieving ability. Lastly, I sough

papers.title: FPGA-Based Neural Network Accelerators for Space Missions: A Survey
papers.summary: Space missions are growing ever more ambitious, placing greater demands on onboard computing. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) have garnered interest due to their reconfigurability and cost-effectiveness. At the same time, neural network (NN)-based methods are proving invaluable for critical spacecraft tasks such as autonomous operations, remote sensing, selective downlink, and data compression. This survey reviews and classifies the state-of-the-art in FPGA-based NN accelerators for space missions. We examine current trends, highlight key challenges, and suggest directions for future research. This work highlights key aspects for integrating high-performance NN acceleration into next-generation spacecraft computing systems.

papers.title: What Were You Thinking? An LLM-Driven Large-Scale Study of Refactoring Motivations in Open Source Projects
papers.summary: Context . Code refactoring improves software quality without changing external behavior. Despite its advantages, its benefits are hindered by the considerable cost of time, resources, and continuous effort it demands. Aim . Understanding why developers refactor, and which metrics capture these motivations, may support wider and more effective use of refactoring in practice. Method . We performed a large-scale empirical study to analyze developers’ refactoring activity, leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to identify underlying motivations from version control data, comparing our findings with previous motivations reported in the literature. Results . LLMs matched human judgment in 80% of cases, but aligned with literature-based motivations in only 47%. They enriched 22% of motivations with more detailed rationale, often highlighting readability, clarity, and structural improvements. Most motivations were pragmatic, focused on simplification and maintainability. While metrics related to developer experience and code readability ranked highest, their correlation with motivation categories was weak. Conclusions . We conclude that LLMs effectively capture surface-level motivations but struggle with architectural reasoning. Their value lies in providing localized explanations, which, when combined with software metrics, can form hybrid approaches. Such integration offers a promi

papers.title: The acmeological gamification framework for creative competence development: a testable theory for pre-service teacher education
papers.summary: Gamification in higher education has been studied mainly as a means of increasing motivation, engagement, and achievement, with far less attention to how game mechanics contribute to the creative competence of pre-service teachers. This article advances the Acmeological Gamification Framework for Creative Competence Development (AGF-CCD), a testable developmental theory of how gamified learning conditions may contribute to creative professional capability in teacher education. The framework was developed through a purposive narrative theory-building synthesis, supported by a mechanism-level evidence map in which empirical studies, syntheses, and theoretical sources are kept apart; it is neither a systematic review nor an empirical validation. It takes the well-supported link from need-supportive mechanics to autonomous motivation as a boundary premise and proposes three sequential links: autonomous motivation is channelled by interpretive feedback into reflective practice and in-task metacognitive regulation (P1); reflective practice under psychological safety and meaningful challenge activates divergent and convergent thinking (P2); and repeated, reflected creative activity in authentic professional tasks consolidates into durable creative competence, evidenced by retention and transfer (P3). papers.title: Discovering High Level Patterns from Simulation Traces
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are unable to reliably reason about specific physical systems. Attempts to imbue LLMs with knowledge of the necessary physics concepts have shown great promise, but explainability and validation remain open challenges. An emerging alternative is tooling, where LLMs can query physical simulators and use the resulting simulation traces as context for validation. This approach suffers from poor scalability since simulation traces contain large volumes of fine-grained numerical and semantic data. We show that translating simulation traces to a sparse representation of ‘high-level’ structural patterns leads to more effective interpretation by LLMs. We propose an unsupervised learning scheme to perform this translation, or annotation, via program synthesis. Our learning results in a library of programs that act as pattern detectors which can translate simulation logs to sparse, annotated pattern sequences. The detected patterns may optionally be guided by human experts via string labels (rigid collision, stretching spring, etc.). papers.title: THE EVOLUTION OF SOCIAL COMMERCE: A HISTORICAL ANALYSIS OF WEBSITE FEATURES AND DIGITAL INTERACTIONS
papers.summary: Social commerce represents one of the most significant transformations in digital retail, merging social media's interactive capabilities with e-commerce transactional functionality. This research traces the evolutionary trajectory of social commerce from its nascent stages in the early 2000s through its current sophisticated implementations, examining how website features and digital interactions have transformed consumer purchasing behavior. Through systematic analysis of platform developments, feature innovations, and user engagement patterns across two decades, we document how social commerce evolved from simple product sharing mechanisms to comprehensive ecosystems integrating user-generated content, live streaming, influencer marketing, and artificial intelligence-driven personalization. Our historical analysis reveals distinct developmental phases: the foundational period (2005-2010) characterized by basic social sharing features, the integration era (2011-2015) marked by dedicated social commerce platforms and Facebook commerce initiatives, the mobile acceleration phase (2016-2019) dominated by Instagram shopping and messaging-based commerce, and the immersive experience period (2020-2024) featuring live commerce, augmented reality try-ons, and community-driven purchasing.
